name: Computer Networks
description: How data crosses a network: layered architecture, the link layer, IP and routing, TCP and UDP, application protocols, and network security.

topics.name: Network Architecture
topics.summary: Layering as the organising idea, and the models that describe it.

subtopics.name: Layered Models
subtopics.summary: The OSI and TCP/IP models and the service each layer provides.

objectives.text: Name the layers of the TCP/IP model and the function of each
Map an OSI layer to its TCP/IP counterpart
Explain why layering makes a network easier to evolve

subtopics.name: Encapsulation and Protocol Data Units
subtopics.summary: Headers added and removed as data descends and ascends the stack.

objectives.text: Describe how a message is encapsulated as it passes down the stack
Identify the PDU name at each layer
Compute protocol overhead for a given payload size

subtopics.name: Network Performance
subtopics.summary: Bandwidth, latency, propagation delay, jitter and throughput.

objectives.text: Distinguish bandwidth from latency and from throughput
Compute total delay from transmission, propagation and queuing components
Explain the bandwidth-delay product and its significance

topics.name: The Link Layer
topics.summary: Getting a frame across one hop reliably, and sharing a medium fairly.

subtopics.name: Framing and Error Detection
subtopics.summary: Frame delimitation, parity, checksums and cyclic redundancy checks.

objectives.text: Compute a checksum or CRC for a given frame
Compare error detection with error correction
Explain why the link layer detects errors even though higher layers also do

subtopics.name: Medium Access Control
subtopics.summary: Sharing a channel: CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA and collisions.

objectives.text: Explain how CSMA/CD detects and recovers from a collision
Describe why wireless networks use collision avoidance rather than detection
Compute the effect of collisions on effective throughput

subtopics.name: Switching and Ethernet
subtopics.summary: MAC addresses, switches, learning bridges and LAN topology.

objectives.text: Explain how a switch learns which port reaches a MAC address
Distinguish a switch from a hub and from a router
Describe the structure of an Ethernet frame

topics.name: The Network Layer
topics.summary: Getting a packet across many hops to a host anywhere on the internet.

subtopics.name: IP Addressing and Subnetting
subtopics.summary: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, subnet masks, CIDR and address exhaustion.

objectives.text: Compute a subnet mask, network address and usable host range from a CIDR prefix
Divide an address block into subnets meeting stated host requirements
Explain the motivation for IPv6 and for network address translation

subtopics.name: Routing
subtopics.summary: Forwarding tables, distance vector and link state routing.

objectives.text: Determine the next hop from a forwarding table using longest prefix match
Compare distance vector with link state routing
Trace the convergence of a distance vector protocol after a link failure

subtopics.name: IP and Supporting Protocols
subtopics.summary: The IP datagram, fragmentation, TTL, ICMP and ARP.

objectives.text: Explain the purpose of the TTL field and the effect of it reaching zero
Describe how ARP resolves an IP address to a MAC address
Explain what ping and traceroute reveal and how they work

topics.name: The Transport Layer
topics.summary: End-to-end delivery between processes, reliable or not.

subtopics.name: UDP and TCP
subtopics.summary: Ports, multiplexing, and the choice between reliability and latency.

objectives.text: Compare UDP and TCP on reliability, ordering and overhead
Explain how port numbers multiplex connections to processes
Choose the appropriate transport protocol for a stated application

subtopics.name: Reliable Data Transfer
subtopics.summary: Acknowledgements, retransmission, sequence numbers and sliding windows.

objectives.text: Explain how sequence numbers and acknowledgements provide reliability
Describe the sliding window mechanism and its effect on throughput
Trace TCP connection establishment and termination

subtopics.name: Flow and Congestion Control
subtopics.summary: Receiver windows, slow start, congestion avoidance and fairness.

objectives.text: Distinguish flow control from congestion control
Describe TCP slow start and congestion avoidance phases
Explain how TCP infers congestion from packet loss

topics.name: The Application Layer
topics.summary: The protocols users actually interact with.

subtopics.name: HTTP and the Web
subtopics.summary: Request/response, methods, status codes, cookies and caching.

objectives.text: Describe the structure of an HTTP request and response
Explain the meaning of common status code classes
Explain how caching reduces load and how it is controlled

subtopics.name: DNS
subtopics.summary: The distributed name hierarchy and the resolution process.

objectives.text: Trace an iterative DNS resolution from root to authoritative server
Explain the role of caching and TTL in DNS
Describe the consequence of a DNS failure for an application

subtopics.name: Other Application Protocols
subtopics.summary: Email, file transfer, streaming and the client-server versus peer-to-peer models.

objectives.text: Compare client-server with peer-to-peer architectures
Describe the protocols involved in sending and retrieving email
Explain the requirements streaming places on the network

topics.name: Network Security
topics.summary: Threats to communication and the mechanisms that counter them.

subtopics.name: Threats and Attacks
subtopics.summary: Eavesdropping, spoofing, man-in-the-middle and denial of service.

objectives.text: Describe how a man-in-the-middle attack is mounted
Explain why an unauthenticated protocol is vulnerable to spoofing
Distinguish a denial-of-service from a distributed denial-of-service attack

subtopics.name: Securing a Channel
subtopics.summary: TLS, certificates and the handshake that establishes trust.

objectives.text: Describe the purpose of each stage of the TLS handshake
Explain the role of a certificate authority in establishing trust
State what TLS does and does not protect

subtopics.name: Firewalls and Network Defence
subtopics.summary: Filtering, network segmentation, VPNs and intrusion detection.

objectives.text: Explain how a packet-filtering firewall makes a decision
Describe the purpose of network segmentation
Compare a VPN with an unencrypted connection over the public internet
